proof:
Source. Step 7 of the parent proof: 'apply the area formula of step 3 to the injective linear map L on ℝ^n. Its derivative is L at every point, so its Jacobian is J_L … and L(ℝ^n) = T.' This is Simon Ch. 2, §3, (3.1) in integral form: H^n(ℓ(A)) = √det(ℓ*∘ℓ) H^n(A) for linear ℓ : ℝ^n → ℝ^{n+k}. It is obtained from the Bochner area formula, SimonGMT Chapter02.integral_area_formula_of_injective_derivative.

1. (Hypotheses of the area formula.) Take the source set s = ℝ^n, which is measurable. A continuous linear map is differentiable everywhere and is its own derivative: DL(x) = L for every x (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.fderiv). Hence DL(x) is injective for every x by hypothesis, and L is injective on ℝ^n.

2. (Area formula.) The Bochner area formula, an identity valid for every integrand, gives ∫_{L(ℝ^n)} f dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] = ∫_{ℝ^n} J_L(x) f(Lx) dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n](x). Here J_L(x) = √det(DL(x)* ∘ DL(x)): SimonGMT's areaJacobianAt L x, rewritten by areaJacobianAt_eq_sqrt_det_adjoint_comp. By step 1, J_L(x) = √det(L* ∘ L) for every x, a constant.

3. (Normalisation.) finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, so both measures are μHE[n]. On ℝ^n, μHE[n] is Lebesgue measure (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume). The restriction of a measure to the whole space is the measure itself. So the right side is ∫_{ℝ^n} √det(L*∘L)·f(Lx) dL^n(x).

4. (Image.) L(ℝ^n) = range L. This set is the one underlying the submodule LinearMap.range L (Mathlib LinearMap.coe_range); the coercion of L to a linear map has the same underlying function (ContinuousLinearMap.coe_coe).

5. (Constant.) For every integrand φ and constant c, ∫ c·φ = c·∫ φ (integral_const_mul). Indeed, if c ≠ 0 then c·φ is integrable iff φ is, and both sides are 0 in the non-integrable case; if c = 0 both sides are 0. Therefore ∫_{range L} f dH^n = √det(L* ∘ L)·∫_{ℝ^n} f(Lb) dL^n(b). ∎
